subject.title: trajectory_runtime_events grows unbounded: 85% of a 2GB production agent DB

question: Which supported retention contract should govern trajectory runtime events: age-based expiry, a per-agent global byte budget, reduced captured payloads, or a defined combination?
rationale: The report shows that the existing per-session cap does not bound total database growth, but the acceptable loss of historical runtime traces and the upgrade treatment for already-large databases are product and observability decisions.

options.title: Bound total storage and reduce payload
options.body: Adopt a per-agent global byte budget with oldest-first eviction and stop persisting recoverable full prompt text, then provide an explicit cleanup path for existing databases.

options.title: Use age-based retention
options.body: Expire trajectory runs after a documented retention period while retaining the present event payload shape.

options.title: Preserve current retention pending policy
options.body: Keep the present per-session-only cap until maintainers define support and observability requirements for historical traces.

recommendation.title: Bound total storage and reduce payload
recommendation.body: Adopt a per-agent global byte budget with oldest-first eviction and stop persisting recoverable full prompt text, then provide an explicit cleanup path for existing databases.

likelyOwner.reason: The reporter supplied the production measurements and the concrete retention alternatives requiring direction.
